subdomain: 1.6 Align solutions to business value pillars (efficiency, transformation, productivity, cost, performance SLAs)

en.question: A workload has three mandatory acceptance limits: task success of at least 98%, end-to-end 95th-percentile latency of at most five seconds, and total cost of at most $0.10 per accepted task. Representative measurements are sufficient for this decision. Design A achieves 97.6%, three seconds, and $0.06; B achieves 98.5%, 4.5 seconds, and $0.08; C achieves 99.2%, 4.8 seconds, and $0.11; D achieves 98.9%, seven seconds, and $0.09. Which recommendation is supported without changing a design?

options.text: Choose A because its lower cost and faster response compensate for the measured task-success shortfall.
options.note: A fails the mandatory quality floor. Better cost and latency cannot compensate for a non-negotiable acceptance constraint.

options.text: Choose C because its higher task success justifies exceeding the agreed cost limit by a small amount.
options.note: C exceeds the stipulated cost ceiling. A quality improvement does not authorize relaxing that mandatory limit.

options.text: Choose B because it meets all three limits; compare improvements only within the feasible set.
options.note: B is the only measured candidate satisfying quality, end-to-end latency, and total cost simultaneously. Preference trade-offs apply after mandatory constraints are met.

options.text: Choose D because its task success and cost meet their limits, making slower responses an acceptable trade-off.
options.note: D violates the mandatory latency ceiling. Meeting the other two limits does not make the user-facing performance requirement optional.
